news.Title: Tesla Just Spent $4.73 Billion on Capex. Here's Where Every Dollar Went.
news.Content:
Tesla 's (NASDAQ: TSLA) capital expenditures (capex) totaled $4.73 billion in Q3, more than double the $2.25 billion it spent a year earlier. That's a substantial increase, although considerably less than the roughly $7.5 billion Wall Street anticipated.

Tesla also reduced its full-year capital spending forecast from more than $25 billion to about $20 billion. But that's still more than twice the $8.53 billion it spent in 2025. So where is all that money going? Let's take a closer look.

Missed AI's "Act 1"? Act 2 Could Be 14x Bigger. Most investors think they missed the AI boat because they didn't buy Nvidia in 2005. But according to our analysts, we're only at the end of "Act 1"—the R&D phase. "Act 2" is the global rollout. Continue »

AI infrastructure and autonomous vehicles

Tesla has been rapidly expanding its artificial intelligence (AI) computing infrastructure at Gigafactory outside of Austin, Texas. This is what's training the neural networks powering full self-driving, Cybercab autonomous vehicles, and Optimus humanoid robots. And it requires thousands of specialized processors, servers, networking equipment, cooling systems, and electrical infrastructure.

Tesla is also investing in Cybercab manufacturing and its robotaxi fleet. Unlike vehicles sold directly to consumers, Tesla robotaxis require up-front investment in vehicles, charging infrastructure, and maintenance infrastructure before generating transportation revenue. The potential payoff is significant.

Estimates from S&P Global Market Intelligence and Visible Alpha suggest Tesla's robotaxi business could generate about $42.4 billion in annual revenue by 2030. At a hypothetical 20% operating margin, that would produce roughly $8.5 billion in annual operating profit.

Tesla could also generate recurring revenue from its full self-driving software. At $99 per month, 5 million paying subscribers would generate about $5.9 billion annually.

Of course, these projections depend on regulatory approvals, technological improvements, and customers adopting the services in substantial numbers. While I'm optimistic on all three fronts, there are no guarantees.

The Optimus advantage

Tesla is also investing in manufacturing capacity for Optimus, its humanoid robot designed to perform physical tasks in factories and other workplaces. In Q3, Tesla began production of Optimus at its Fremont, California, facility, where it's converting manufacturing space previously used for the Model S and Model X vehicles.

The company has discussed eventually producing as many as 1 million robots annually at Fremont. But getting there will require significant investment in production lines, motors, sensors, batteries, and specialized manufacturing equipment. And that stuff isn't cheap.

Story Continues

Tesla Chief Executive Officer Elon Musk has previously suggested that Optimus could eventually cost about $20,000 to $30,000 per robot to manufacture at scale. At a hypothetical selling price of $30,000 per robot, annual sales of 500,000 robots would generate $15 billion in revenue, while 1 million robots would generate $30 billion.

Energy storage is already producing results

Unlike robotics and robotaxis, Tesla's energy storage business already has an established customer base. In Q3, the company deployed 13.7 gigawatt-hours of energy storage products, up about 10% year over year. Tesla also began production at its new Megafactory in Brookshire, Texas, which has a planned annual capacity of 50 gigawatt-hours.

If you're unfamiliar, these large battery systems help utilities store electricity, stabilize electrical grids, and provide backup power. So as you can imagine, demand from AI data centers is creating another potential growth opportunity.

Tesla reported its highest-ever energy storage order rate and backlog during the quarter. It also began shipping Megapacks using domestically manufactured lithium-iron-phosphate battery cells from Nevada.

Semiconductor manufacturing adds another expense

Tesla is also pursuing its ambitious Terafab semiconductor project in Texas, which will support future AI computing requirements. Manufacturing advanced chips requires expensive fabrication equipment, specialized facilities, and substantial technical expertise.

Tesla hasn't disclosed a complete cost breakdown for these plans, so at this point, we don't know how much of its projected capital spending will ultimately go toward semiconductor manufacturing.

Can Tesla afford all this spending?

Tesla generated $6.26 billion in operating cash flow during Q3. After capital expenditures, free cash flow reached $1.53 billion. The company also finished the quarter with about $45.4 billion in cash and investments. However, net income declined 43% to $787 million, while revenue remained essentially unchanged at $28.1 billion.

The revised $20 billion annual capital spending forecast suggests Tesla is becoming more selective about how quickly it deploys capital. That's encouraging from a cash management perspective, but slower investment could also delay product commercialization.

Still, Tesla's long-term potential remains solid. Robotaxis, Optimus, and AI software could eventually generate billions in additional revenue, while energy storage is already expanding. But spending billions doesn't guarantee those businesses will become profitable.

Indeed, the next few years will determine whether Tesla's investments produce returns large enough to justify their cost. But given Musk's history of turning big ideas that were once considered impossible into reality, I remain bullish.

Missed AI's "Act 1"? Act 2 Could Be 14x Bigger

Most investors think they missed the AI boat because they didn't buy Nvidia in 2005.

But according to our analysts, we're only at the end of "Act 1"—the R&D phase. "Act 2" is the global rollout, a massive technology build-out that Google's CEO says could be more profound than fire or electricity.

While everyone watches the chip designers, one "backbone" company provides the critical technology that Nvidia and AMD literally cannot function without. We've detailed this under-the-radar player in our new AI Playbook.

Continue »

news.Title: GM is pitching itself more as a tech company like Tesla
news.Content:
If you can't beat tech companies, join them. General Motors ( GM ) said Tuesday it will move its stock listing from the New York Stock Exchange to the Nasdaq, home of many of Silicon Valley's biggest names, in an effort to repitch the legacy Detroit automaker as a tech-forward enterprise.

Even sitting close to names like Apple ( AAPL ) and Amazon ( AMZN ) can have a spillover effect, as investors cling to the excitement around AI and tech's overall influence in steering the market. Labels matter — remember Domino's ( DPZ ) identity as " a technology company that happens to sell pizza ?"

Walmart ( WMT ), another name you might not associate with cutting-edge tech, made the same change to the Nasdaq earlier this year as it embraces its own AI and advertising transformation.

"GM's customer-focused, technology-driven strategy is creating value for our stockholders, making Nasdaq a natural home for our listing as we grow," said Paul Jacobson, the company's CFO, in a statement on Tuesday.

The undisputed heavyweight champion of this move is Elon Musk. Tesla ( TSLA ) hasn't been a "car company" for years — certainly if you look at its valuation — and SpaceX ( SPCX ) is no longer a rocket company. (Still, GM has done well.)

And investors have bought these arguments. Both companies have valuations commensurate with being an AI/robotics/robotaxi giant or an AI/datacenter/chipmaker giant. A much-talked-about merger with SpaceX would put an even finer point on what Tesla is.

Of course, GM does not have these activities to make its case.

But in some respects the shift makes sense. Newer vehicles have enhanced safety and steering features that make driving meaningfully different than sitting behind the wheel of the car you got your license in. GM, like other automakers, is outfitting its vehicles with more sophisticated software and sensors. The company announced last week it's working to reduce its development cycle by half through AI tools and virtualization.

Some observers are skeptical of the new sales pitch, however.

"Cars are the first robots out there in the wild," Envorso founder Adrian Balfour said on Yahoo Finance's Morning Hang on Tuesday. "If it was a data play or if it was a robotics play, I could really see it. But without that, I'm not sure."

Hamza Shaban is a reporter for Yahoo Finance covering markets and the economy. Follow Hamza on X @hshaban .

news.Title: Google, Microsoft, and Amazon have to justify the AI spending boom this week
news.Content:
Google ( GOOG , GOOGL ), Microsoft ( MSFT ), and Amazon ( AMZN ) have one big, collective task on their digital shoulders this week as they report their quarterly earnings: They need to justify the AI spending boom.

The stakes are high — these companies lead a week of corporate results that account for more than a third of the S&P 500's ( ^GSPC ) earnings

Like Meta ( META ) before them, the biggest question they'll face is likely about AI spending . Specifically, what that number is and how it compares to the expected returns.

"All eyes will be on AI monetization vs. spending, with hyperscalers' 2027 capex estimates already revised up by nearly 90% YTD," Bank of America strategist Savita Subramanian wrote in a note on Tuesday.

Tech execs having to justify their huge AI spending has been a feature of earnings reports for the past two years. Skeptical investors are eager to see returns on investment, and Wall Street has been rattled by cycles of doubt. But conditions in the economy and the investing environments have changed , heightening the urgency to show results.

The recent tech sell-off has thrown AI financing into the spotlight. Companies leading the data center build-out have flagged. And investors have expressed mixed feelings about tech giants like Meta selling shares and borrowing to finance their AI ambitions .

The massive demand for financing has increased the competition for capital. That has put pressure on tech companies to preemptively raise enormous sums of money, especially as Wall Street prepares to shepherd the blockbuster IPOs of two frontier AI labs — Anthropic ( ANTH.PVT ) as soon as next month and OpenAI ( OPAI.PVT ) likely next year.

AI business dynamics are also changing. The era of tokenmaxxing is officially over. Businesses are becoming pickier and choosier with their AI spending — scaling back, using less expensive models, and experimenting with different services. The slowdown in token spending among corporations suggests the lavish appetite for compute only existed when it was effectively free. And so, if the demand for compute isn't infinite and is actually price-sensitive, that means justifying AI costs will be more important.

Lastly, Meta's Muse and the early success of personal assistant AI agents have scrambled product priorities. Meta has reoriented the entire company around the division behind Muse and envisions its operations becoming a massive service network and revenue engine. The cash might not come now or even soon, but it will flow, the bull thesis goes.

Zuckerberg might have a mixed record, but his company is behind him. And he had the benefit of moving first. The other tech giants this week will have to come up with answers too.

news.Title: 台積電鳳凰城廠周邊工業區需大量資金投入  「大地主」來台灣尋金主
news.Content:
台積電（2330）大手筆斥資5兆元赴美國亞歷桑那州投資，總計將在鳳凰城北部蓋12座廠，連帶18家設備廠、供應鍊一齊「東進」，錢潮帶動人潮，湧進全美第五大城市，也為工業用土等當地不動產開發帶來龐大商機與資金需求，吸引擁地緊臨 TSMC廠的「大地主」土地開發商之一、北美資產管理公司ICM Asset Management（以下簡稱ICM）高層紛紛來台尋金主。

「台灣人最了解台積電！」ICM來台三大誘因

成立20餘年的北美資產管理公司ICM 及旗下美國子公司ICM Realty Group今（28）日宣布與康和投顧展開合作，聚焦美國陽光帶工業不動產市場，分享其對半導體、先進製造、航太國防及物流產業發展趨勢的觀察。此次特別來台尋金主，主要三大誘因。一是台灣人最了解台積電。二、台灣科技股大漲，科技老闆滿手現金，加上三是亞灣專區設立，亦吸引國際資產管理公司來台。

根據ICM提供的2026年第三季市場資料，鳳凰城都會區就業人口約250萬人，過去一年增加約2.4萬個工作機會，人口成長速度約為全美平均的四倍。工業不動產市場方面，鳳凰城2026年第三季空置率降至10.3%；過去12個月淨吸納量達2,050萬平方英尺，超過同期新增供給900萬平方英尺的兩倍。其中，面積達30萬平方英尺以上的大型工業設施空置率為5.1%，反映大型製造及物流業者仍具空間需求。

好市多及萬豪酒店今年第四季進駐北鳳凰城

鄰近台積電鳳凰城北部廠區的Halo Vista大型開發計畫，規畫涵蓋工業製造、辦公、零售、住宅及教育等多元用途，整體開發面積最高可達3,000萬平方英尺（約279萬平方公尺）；首期工業開發計畫預計興建七棟建築，總面積約78萬平方英尺（約7.25萬平方公尺）。

同時包括Costco好市多及萬豪酒店Marriote今年第四季也打算進駐該地區。該區域開放需要龐大資金需求，對吸引不動產開發及相關資產管理公司相繼來台。

ICM過去多筆鳳凰城土地開發投報率驚人

ICM發跡自德國，以美加不動產開放為主力，甚至涵蓋擁有瑪麗亞凱麗等知名巨星音樂版權專利投資，資產規模超過21億美元，擁有2萬多名投資人，過去亦曾在鳳凰城地區參與多項工業不動產開發。

其中ICM在鳳凰城北部包括位於西谷地區Loop 303交通廊帶、面積約27萬平方英尺的Glendale Industrial開發案，以及位於10號州際公路沿線、由兩棟建築組成、面積約25萬平方英尺的Buckeye Industrial開發案，分別於2022年及2024年出售，內部報酬率IRR曾一度高達66%及24%之多。

此外，ICM亦曾與Mack Real Estate成立合資事業，參與鄰近台積電鳳凰城廠區的Mack Innovation Park開發計畫，累積從投資機會辨識、土地開發、招商租賃至資產處分等實務經驗。

ICM Asset Management執行長、合夥人暨投資組合經理John Courtliff表示，ICM很高興與康和投顧展開合作，並期待將深耕北美多年的工業不動產經驗與市場觀察帶到台灣。他指出，鳳凰城的長期人口與就業成長，加上半導體、先進製造、航太國防及科技產業發展，正形成具實際企業需求支撐的工業市場。

南部「陽光帶」科技廊帶 德州、北卡南卡亦受矚

随著美國總統川普大喊「讓美國再次偉大」，製造業紛紛回流美國，ICM也看好美國陽光帶地區具有人口成長、企業遷入及產業投資等長期動能，德州奧斯汀及周邊成長廊帶受到科技與半導體產業發展帶動，三星電子位於泰勒市興建中的半導體廠，也為當地工業及物流市場帶來新的產業需求。佛羅里達州奧蘭多具備航太國防及工業發展基礎；北卡羅來納州及南卡羅來納州則受惠於港口物流、汽車與航太供應鏈，以及製造業持續移入。上述地區與喬治亞州共同構成美國陽光帶重要的產業及物流網絡。

ICM Asia共同董事總經理Pablo Romero表示，鳳凰城、奧斯汀、喬治亞州及南北卡羅來納州等市場，正處於科技發展、人口成長與工業需求交會的位置。ICM在北美工業不動產領域累積的經驗，也將成為其深化亞洲市場交流的重要基礎。

黎奕彬：台積電帶台灣資產管理走向全世界

康和投顧董事長黎奕彬表示，台積電走向全球，不僅展現台灣產業的實力，也在海外帶動新的供應鏈及實體資產需求。此次與ICM合作，讓康和能以更宏觀的視角掌握台積電全球布局所帶動的產業發展，同時進一步強化國際視野與專業能力。康和也將持續響應政府推動亞洲資產管理中心政策，結合國際專業與在地能力，為台灣資產管理產業的深化與發展貢獻力量。

news.Title: 5 Stocks Poised to Win Big as SpaceX Ramps Up AI Infrastructure
news.Content:
Space Exploration Technologies (NASDAQ: SPCX) just upped the ante in the artificial intelligence (AI) infrastructure race, planning to increase its computing capacity by about 10 gigawatts next year, with a moonshot goal of boosting it by 20 gigawatts. That's a huge amount of spending, with Nvidia (NASDAQ: NVDA), SK Hynix (NASDAQ: SKHY), Vertiv (NYSE: VRT), Amphenol (NYSE: APH), and Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing (NYSE: TSM) among the biggest beneficiaries.

Let's look at how each of these artificial intelligence stocks could benefit.

Missed AI's "Act 1"? Act 2 Could Be 14x Bigger. Most investors think they missed the AI boat because they didn't buy Nvidia in 2005. But according to our analysts, we're only at the end of "Act 1"—the R&D phase. "Act 2" is the global rollout. Continue »

1. Nvidia

Nvidia will be the biggest beneficiary of SpaceX's AI infrastructure spree. SpaceX will build its data centers exclusively using Nvidia's Vera Rubin architecture, which means the semiconductor company will supply virtually all the chips and networking for this enormous build-out.

Nvidia gets roughly $40 billion per gigawatt from Vera Rubin, so this could be a $400 billion-plus revenue boost if it doesn't take capacity away from other customers. The current analyst average estimate is for Nvidia to generate roughly $412 billion in revenue this fiscal year (ending January 2027), so this would be a gigantic one-year order from SpaceX.

2. SK Hynix

Without high bandwidth memory (HBM), Nvidia's ultra-expensive graphics processing units (GPUs) can't deliver their full potential in handling AI workloads. As such, HBM has become essential to the AI build-out. However, HBM is currently in short supply, and memory companies' ability to quickly increase supply is limited by their capacity to purchase more extreme ultraviolet (EUV) lithography machines, which are used to make the critical components in both HBM and advanced logic chips, such as GPUs and central processing units (CPUs). This has resulted in a major supply-demand imbalance across the entire memory market, leading to skyrocketing prices across the board.

SK Hynix (NASDAQ: SKHY), meanwhile, looks to be the memory company most likely to benefit from SpaceX's increased AI infrastructure spending, as it is the HBM leader with more than 50% market share and a close relationship with Nvidia. The two companies already have a $500 billion long-term supply deal in place, and SpaceX's spending will only increase demand for HBM and memory in an already constrained market.

Story Continues

3. Vertiv

AI data centers require substantial power delivery and heat removal, which is where Vertiv comes in, providing data center cooling and power management infrastructure. On its Q3 earnings call, SpaceX cited cooling and power as one of the biggest bottlenecks the industry faces. However, it said it has a plan to get to 20 gigawatts of power and cooling equipment by the end of next year.

Although it is not confirmed that Vertiv is a direct supplier to SpaceX's AI data centers, the company should at the very least benefit from increased industry demand in another AI infrastructure market currently facing supply shortages.

4. Amphenol

Amphenol provides power distribution hardware and interconnects that allow data centers to operate at high speeds. Although the company has a wide customer base across industries, data centers are its largest market. Amphenol is a key supply partner to Nvidia and provides important components for Nvidia's Vera Rubin NVL72 system.

The stock is a favorite of Evercore ISI, and analyst Amit Daryanani recently highlighted the company as one of the biggest potential winners from SpaceX's planned AI computing capacity.

5. Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing

Any increase in AI infrastructure capital expenditure is generally good news for Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing. The company has a virtual monopoly in manufacturing advanced logic chips, including Nvidia's GPUs and CPUs. As such, SpaceX's significant spending on AI infrastructure next year will be beneficial.

The bigger long-term question will be the impact of SpaceX and Tesla 's huge planned chip manufacturing facility, Terafab. Elon Musk has said it could start producing chips in volume by Q3 2028, although his track record with timeline predictions isn't the best. TSMC and Musk have talked about TSMC getting involved in the project, but there seems to be a disagreement over who would run the facility. As such, SpaceX's spending will benefit TSMC in 2027, but over the longer term, it's still up in the air.

news.Title: 外資買超台股159億元加碼ETF　連14日減碼台積電聯發科
news.Content:
（中央社記者鍾榮峰台北2026年10月28日電）台股今天上漲939點收47035點，重返季線並收復47000點，外資及陸資轉買超台股新台幣159.22億元，投信連12買，自營商終結連12賣。外資加碼主動ETF、面板以及OEM代工族群，不過連14日減碼台積電和聯發科。

三大法人外資及陸資、投信、自營商同步買超，合計買超298.94億元，其中自營商買超21.65億元，投信買超118.07億元。在台指期淨部位，三大法人淨多單增加2282口至2745口，其中外資淨空單減少1126口至8萬4917口。

觀察外資買賣超個股動向，根據台灣證券交易所統計，外資買超逾萬張的股票包括主動中信台灣收益（00406A）、友達、主動統一升級50（00403A）、華邦電、群創、力積電、中信台日韓PCB（009828）、聯電、仁寶、鴻海、英業達、南亞、群益台灣精選高息（00919）等。

相較之下，外資今天減碼逾萬張的股票僅旺宏、台玻、寶成等3檔。外資調節台積電3175張，累計連14個交易日賣超台積電近15.6萬張。外資也減碼聯發科1037張，連14日賣超累計達3.51萬張。

啟發投顧副總經理容逸燊接受記者電訪指出，美國11月上旬期中選舉前，股市表現仍趨量縮震盪，本週美國聯邦準備理事會（Fed）將公布利率決策動向，10月底對沖基金會計結算，部分資金近期撤出亞洲股市回流美股，預期美期中選舉過後，部分資金有機會重回亞股，短線台股在45000點至46000點區間有強力支撐。

觀察外資在台股期現貨市場動向，容逸燊表示，外資近2日在台股現貨市場減碼幅度縮手，在台指期淨空單部位降至8.5萬口以下，外資態度並未持續偏空。

台新臺灣中小主動式ETF基金經理人沈建宏表示，台股在10月初來到近5萬點歷史高點，不過漲勢集中在少數族群且輪動速度快，包括美公債殖利率、美聯準會利率動向等因素，仍對股市帶來壓力，不過包括市場對AI產業部分雜音，屬於短期影響，長期企業獲利上修趨勢不變。

news.Title: SK Hynix, Nvidia and Micron send one clear message to investors with their stocks off the highs
news.Content:
Some of the biggest players in the AI trade are sending a clear message to investors who have watched their stock prices fall off record highs.

That message is that the sell-offs are unwarranted, and they will use stock buybacks to boost shareholder returns.

After reporting a sixth straight quarter of record sales and profits on Wednesday, SK Hynix ( SKHY ) said it would repurchase 30 trillion won (about $22 billion) of its stock this year. This follows a 40 trillion won buyback program announced in August.

SK Hynix shares rose 7% in pre-market trading. They had fallen 24% in the month before the earnings release.

With its stock down about 14% in the past month, Micron ( MU ) is also planning to be a big purchaser of its stock soon.

The memory chip giant said in its 10-K filing earlier this month that its board authorized discretionary share repurchases of up to $35.16 billion. This marks the largest buyback ceiling in the company's history.

Micron is expected to begin buying back its stock after Dec. 9, when restrictions related to the Chips Act lift.

And the king of AI chips Nvidia ( NVDA ) isn't standing idly by on the buyback front. Its stock is down 3% in the past month and has traded sideways for six months.

In late September, Nvidia issued a stunning new $150 billion stock buyback plan, the largest share repurchase authorization increase in history. It brings the company's total buyback authorization to $235 billion.

"We believe the expanded buyback reinforces NVIDIA's view that strong AI-driven free cash flow growth can support both strategic investments and substantial shareholder returns," Citi analyst Atif Malik said.

Brian Sozzi is Yahoo Finance's Executive Editor, host of the Sozzi Unleashed morning show, the ' Power Players With Brian Sozzi' podcast and a member of Yahoo Finance's editorial leadership team.

news.Title: 4 Reasons American Express Stock Is Having Its Worst Year Since 2015 Despite Record Earnings
news.Content:
On Oct. 23, American Express (NYSE: AXP) delivered excellent third-quarter 2026 results and raised its full-year guidance. The financial services giant is forecasting a record $18.30 to $18.60 in full-year earnings per share ($17.60 to $17.90 adjusted) and another year of 10% revenue growth. The midpoint of American Express's adjusted earnings guidance is a 15.4% increase over 2025.

Given the impeccable results, it may seem strange that American Express is down 15.3% year to date. If that level holds, it would be the worst annual decline since 2015.

Missed Nvidia in 2009? This Rare Signal Is Flashing Again. In 2009, a "Double Down" signal flashed for a little-known chipmaker called Nvidia. For the first time in years, that same "Total Conviction" signal is flashing for a company 1/100th the size of Nvidia. Continue »

Here are four reasons American Express is selling off, and whether the financial stock is a buy anyway.

1. American Express stock was red hot entering 2026

Over the last decade, American Express has delivered a 452.8% total return, compared with 322.1% for the S&P 500 (SNPINDEX: ^GSPC), while its earnings have nearly tripled. And in the last three years, American Express is up 137.6% while its earnings are up 47%.

So, despite American Express's excellent results, the simplest reason why it's underperforming in 2026 is probably just a decade-long, mostly uninterrupted surge in the stock price that outpaced earnings growth, leaving American Express prone to a pullback.

2. Margin compression

Another factor affecting American Express is rising expenses that have eroded its margins.

AXP Revenue (TTM) data by YCharts

As you can see in the chart, American Express's revenue and earnings have skyrocketed, but its gross margins are steadily ticking down.

In its latest quarter, card member reward expenses jumped 10% year-over-year, business development was up 11%, and card member services jumped 36%. Total expenses were up 9%, matching the 9% year-over-year increase in revenue. But the fact remains that American Express is spending heavily on customer engagement, which could weigh on margins if cardholder spending weakens.

3. A consumer spending slowdown

Some investors may be worried that American Express's affluent customer base could eventually feel the impact of a higher cost of living and inflationary pressures. It's no secret that consumer spending has been strained by higher costs for household goods, rising utility bills, gas prices, and a massive slowdown in housing and home improvement. American Express's customers continue to spend at a healthy rate, but that may be partly due to strong employment and near-record-high levels in real estate and the stock market .

Story Continues

If asset prices cool off or unemployment ticks up in high-paying jobs because of an economic slowdown or an artificial intelligence (AI) disruption, American Express's core customer base could be affected. Higher interest rates act as a natural brake on economic growth and consumer spending, which in turn affects the outlook for cardholder spending in 2027.

American Express's business model is built around incentivizing customers to make as many of their purchases as possible using their American Express card(s). So if overall spending comes down, it will impact the fees American Express collects from merchants based on transaction volume, interest expenses on outstanding balances, and the annual fees on its pricey cards.

4. AI and agentic commerce

Yet another reason American Express stock could be under pressure is its AI strategy. American Express CEO Stephen Squeri talked at length on the Oct. 23 earnings call about the company's plans to leverage AI efficiency improvements across its operations and the rise of AI and agentic commerce. This basically means having AI agents make purchasing decisions, such as using an American Express card, on behalf of the cardholder.

Squeri believes that American Express is uniquely positioned to win with agentic commerce and using AI to enhance the customer experience because of American Express's connection with the customer, which includes its first-party data, security, closed-loop network, and other advantages.

American Express issues its own cards and has a suite of financial services, from loans to high-yield savings accounts and more. Whereas Visa and Mastercard operate open-loop networks, meaning other banks and financial institutions issue the cards and manage the credit risk.

While Squeri is absolutely right that American Express has a unique opportunity to tap more deeply into each customer's spending habits and preferences, investors may be concerned that American Express's AI budget could further erode its margins. Or that pursuing these AI investments at the expense of reducing employee headcount is the wrong move. In Q3, American Express took a $336 million restructuring charge following a 5% reduction in its global employee headcount.

American Express is too cheap to ignore

Given the strength of American Express's business model, record revenue and earnings, strong growth rates, a loyal customer base, and excellent credit quality, investors may be scratching their heads as to why American Express has gotten so cheap. The stock trades at just 17.8 times the low end of its adjusted 2026 earnings guidance.

While American Express is prone to a consumer spending slowdown and could see further margin pressure from higher costs, the long-term fundamentals of the business are as good as ever. I also think that American Express is uniquely positioned to tap into the emerging agentic commerce industry, given its engaged customer base.

All told, the downward pressure on the stock price is driven by fears of what could happen rather than by the results themselves. This gives long-term investors an incredible opportunity to scoop up American Express shares while they are out of favor.

news.Title: 10 Stocks Warren Buffett and His Successor, Greg Abel, Plan to Hold Forever
news.Content:
It's a new era for Berkshire Hathaway (NYSE:BRKA)(NYSE:BRKB). On Dec. 31, longtime CEO Warren Buffett retired, paving the way for his understudy, Greg Abel, to take over. Berkshire's new boss wasted little time making his mark, dumping 16 stocks in the first quarter , as well as piling into tech titan Alphabet (NASDAQ:GOOGL)(NASDAQ:GOOG).

But despite these changes, one fundamental truth remains: Buffett's and Abel's long-term vision.

Missed AI's "Act 1"? Act 2 Could Be 14x Bigger. Most investors think they missed the AI boat because they didn't buy Nvidia in 2005. But according to our analysts, we're only at the end of "Act 1"—the R&D phase. "Act 2" is the global rollout. Continue »

Warren Buffett and Greg Abel have a list of companies they never plan to sell. Image source: Getty Images.

10 stocks Berkshire Hathaway may never sell

In Warren Buffett's 2023 letter to shareholders, and in Greg Abel's first-ever letter to shareholders, Berkshire's bosses outlined several stocks they planned to effectively hold forever. Warren Buffett labeled the following eight companies as "indefinite" holdings:

Coca-Cola (NYSE:KO)

American Express (NYSE:AXP)

Occidental Petroleum (NYSE:OXY)

Mitsubishi (OTC:MTSUY)

Mitsui (OTC:MITSY)

Itochu (OTC:ITOCY)

Marubeni (OTC:MARUY)

Sumitomo (OTC:SSUMY)

Meanwhile, in Abel's letter to shareholders, he expected four companies to "compound over decades." This includes Coca-Cola and Amex, as well as:

Apple (NASDAQ:AAPL)

Moody's (NYSE:MCO)

Legacy holdings aren't going anywhere

Arguably, the least surprising names on this list are Coca-Cola, American Express, and Moody's, which are the three longest-tenured holdings in Berkshire Hathaway's investment portfolio. Coke, Amex, and Moody's have been continuously held since 1988, 1991, and 2000, respectively.

Aside from having rock-solid operating models, the lure of this trio is their mouthwatering yields on cost. Berkshire Hathaway's minuscule cost bases in Coca-Cola ($3.2475 per share), American Express ($8.489 per share), and Moody's ($10.05 per share) have translated into annual yields relative to cost of 65%, 45%, and 41%, respectively. There's simply no reason for Abel to ever sell this trio.

Image source: Getty Images.

Japan is a big investment theme for Abel

Although Warren Buffett's shareholder letter labeled Japan's five trading houses -- Mitsubishi, Mitsui, Itochu, Marubeni, and Sumitomo -- as indefinite holdings, the sogo shosha, as they're more commonly known, have been a longtime favorite investment theme for Berkshire's newest boss.

Story Continues

Like the Oracle of Omaha, Greg Abel has always been a stickler for value. With U.S. stocks entering 2026 at their second-priciest valuation in history, finding value domestically has been a challenge. However, Japan's sogo shosha have traded at considerably more attractive price-to-earnings (P/E) multiples than U.S. stocks.

Furthermore, Japan's five trading houses all offer impressive capital-return programs, including dividends and share buybacks, as well as modest executive compensation packages. The sogo shosha have built a shareholder-first, long-term mentality that Abel and Buffett appreciate.

Berkshire's No. 1 holding should stick around

Despite Warren Buffett dumping 75% of Berkshire's Apple stake in the nine quarters leading up to his retirement, Abel's first letter to shareholders makes it clear that his company's No. 1 holding isn't going anywhere.

On the one hand, Apple isn't the bargain it once was. When Buffett began building his company's stake in the iPhone maker in early 2016, Apple was oscillating between 10 and 15 times trailing 12-month earnings. Today, Apple commands a P/E ratio of almost 40!

But Abel gravitates toward tech stocks and innovation far more than Warren Buffett ever did as CEO. It also doesn't hurt that Apple has the largest share repurchase program on the planet!

news.Title: Alphabet, Microsoft to report; Fed decision ahead - what’s moving markets
news.Content:
Investing.com - Futures linked to the main U.S. stock indices hover around both sides of the flatline, as investors prepare for a raft of key tech sector earnings and a key Federal Reserve interest rate decision. Alphabet and Microsoft are scheduled to kick off a parade of major tech-sector earnings after the closing bell, while South Korea's SK Hynix reports a sharp jump in quarterly operating profit. Meanwhile, traders will be searching for clues into the Fed's rate outlook following the central bank's latest policy announcement.

Still guessing which stocks will beat the market? Our AI portfolio updates monthly and is outperforming the S&P 500 by 118%. See this month's list »

1. Futures mixed

U.S. stock futures were mixed on Wednesday. By 04:02 ET (08:02 GMT), the S&P 500 futures contract had risen by 10 points, or 0.1%, Nasdaq 100 futures had climbed by 173 points, or 0.6%, and Dow futures had dipped by 117 points, or 0.2%.

The main averages on Wall Street all advanced in the prior session, with tech stocks in particular powering a 1.18% jump in the Nasdaq Composite. A slew of recent artificial intelligence funding deals, as well as Claude-maker Anthropic's long-awaited IPO filing earlier this week, have helped to soothe jitters around massive debt-fueled spending on AI infrastructure.

"[I]nvestors continue to celebrate the AI funding announcements that hit the tape over the last 36 hours [...] as these demonstrate that plenty of money still exists to underwrite the data center bonanza," analysts at Vital Knowledge wrote in a note.

At the same time, the quarterly corporate earnings season is roughly a third over. Results have largely been "decent" thanks to resilient demand, cost controls, and price hikes, the Vital Knowledge analysts said.

2. Big-name tech earnings loom large

Although the AI anxieties of recent weeks were given a reprieve this week, a major test of the AI boom is due to come after the closing bell.

Google-owner Alphabet and software giant Microsoft are set to headline the slate of post-market earnings -- and potentially shed more light on the AI spending outlook among some of the world's largest companies.

In particular, traders are hunting for any signs of possible returns from Big Tech's planned expenditures -- in some cases ranging into the hundreds of billions of dollars -- on the data centers and chips underpinning AI systems.

Altogether, Alphabet, Microsoft and Amazon -- which reports after the bell on Thursday -- are aiming to shell out as much as $600 billion in capital expenditures this year alone.

Story Continues

Whether investors will welcome or balk at an increase to those spending forecasts may be a central question when the firms report this week. Earlier this month, an uptick in Facebook-owner Meta Platforms' spending plans cast a pall over otherwise strong results, sending shares down a day later. Meta's stock is now down by more than 4% so far this year.

"The more skeptical the market gets about AI returns, the harder it becomes to justify today's pace of spending. Meta is a good example: the core business was shown to be strong, but with capex hitting nearly $34 billion in a single quarter, the market increasingly needs to see the ROI from that investment," said Jake Behan, Head of Capital Markets at Direxion.

3. SK Hynix operating profit surges

To that end, SK Hynix posted a stronger-than-expected third-quarter operating profit on Wednesday, with the South Korean memory chip giant outlining plans to return a total of 100 trillion won ($75.5 billion) to shareholders this year.

Unsure what to buy ahead of earnings? Our AI's recent pre-earnings calls delivered gains of +77% to +118% after results dropped. See this month's earnings picks »

Shares of the company jumped over 10% in Seoul trade.

SK Hynix's operating profit for the three months to September 30 surged 632% versus a year ago to 83.33 trillion won, handily beating Bloomberg estimates of 77.5 trillion won.

Revenue spiked 328% to a record 104.615 trillion won, while net income jumped 216% to 39.78 trillion won, SK Hynix said in a statement.

The company, which is among the world's largest memory chipmakers and has been a major beneficiary of the AI era, said it will pursue shareholder returns of 100 trillion won for the year.

4. Fed decision ahead

How investors feel about AI debt deals and spending binges could also be swayed by Wednesday's all-important Fed interest rate decision.

The central bank is tipped to leave rates unchanged after policymakers lifted borrowing costs for the first time since 2023 in September. However, there is currently a three-in-four chance that the Fed opts to raise rates again at its final meeting of the year in December.

For that reason, analysts have suggested that Fed Chair Kevin Warsh's post-decision press conference will receive especially close scrutiny. Yet don't hold your breath for clear-cut guidance: Warsh has long resisted laying out forward guidance.

Still, some of Warsh's colleagues at the Fed have indicated that more hikes may be necessary to quell elevated inflationary pressures.

For tech, more policy tightening could "raise the cost of funding the AI buildout while simultaneously raising the hurdle for the returns needed to justify it," Direxion's Behan flagged.

5. U.S. warns Gulf countries of Iran war renewal after midterms - WSJ

A key driver of rate expectations in recent months have been oil prices, which have soared largely because of disruptions to Middle East supplies following the outbreak of the Iran war in late February.

The increase in crude has pushed up the costs of items like diesel and gasoline. Economists are now on the lookout for any indication that these price jumps, which can impact everything from transportation expenses to consumer gas prices, are feeding into other goods and services.

Although markets have cheered a fresh diplomatic effort to avoid fresh fighting in Iran, the conflict has spread across the Middle East and has shown little sign of de-escalating. Indeed, the U.S. has told Gulf Arab countries to be ready for a short, intense military campaign following the American midterm elections in November, The Wall Street Journal reported.

Benchmark Brent crude futures were last higher by 1.2% at $115.29 a barrel.

news.Title: OpenAI Plans to Buy Google's Chips as Part of Its AI Build-Out
news.Content:
(Bloomberg) -- OpenAI ( OPAI.PVT ) intends to buy artificial intelligence computing chips from Alphabet Inc.'s Google ( GOOG ), according to a person familiar with the matter, part of broader efforts by the ChatGPT maker to build out its AI infrastructure.

Most Read from Bloomberg

Finland and Norway Hold 'Frank' Call With Putin on Ukraine

Lula Wins Record Fourth Term in Surprise Brazil Comeback

US to Take In Bolsonaro After He Loses Election and Flees Brazil

Anthropic Files for IPO in Global Race to Raise Cash for AI

Final terms of any deal aren't yet known, according to the person, who asked not to be identified because the discussions are private. OpenAI and Google declined to comment.

The move reflects OpenAI's multipronged bid to quickly add more AI processing power. The company has already announced plans to start using its own chips to support its artificial intelligence models later this year. It joins a stampede of companies working to develop homegrown AI chips and challenge Nvidia Corp.'s dominance in the field.

OpenAI's in-house Jalapeno chips, developed with Broadcom Inc., were created with help from Google veterans. Richard Ho, who runs the OpenAI internal chip team, was previously involved in the development of Google's semiconductors — known as tensor processing units, or TPUs.

Google began working on its TPUs more than a decade ago. Initially, the processors were used to speed up the company's web search engine and improve efficiency.

But the chips soon proved valuable for handling AI work and have emerged in recent years as an alternative to Nvidia's much-prized graphics processing units.

Oracle Corp. also announced on Tuesday that TPUs would be available through its cloud-computing infrastructure.

"The next generation of AI will require a diverse range of compute," Google executive Amin Vahdat said in a statement announcing that deal.

The Information previously reported that OpenAI was planning to buy Google chips.

news.Title: 2 Popular AI Stocks to Sell Before They Drop 57% and 60%, According to Wall Street Analysts
news.Content:
Palantir Technologies (NASDAQ:PLTR) and Super Micro Computer (NASDAQ:SMCI) are popular artificial intelligence stocks. Since January 2023, Palantir has added 3,000% and Super Micro has advanced 325%. But the Wall Street analysts below think the stocks are overvalued.

Brent Thill at Jefferies recommends selling Palantir. His target price of $80 per share implies 60% downside from its current share price of $199.

Mehdi Hosseini at Susquehanna recommends selling Super Micro. His target price of $15 per share implies 57% downside from the current share price of $35.

Here's what investors should know about these popular AI stocks.

Missed Nvidia in 2009? This Rare Signal Is Flashing Again. In 2009, a "Double Down" signal flashed for a little-known chipmaker called Nvidia. For the first time in years, that same "Total Conviction" signal is flashing for a company 1/100th the size of Nvidia. Continue »

Image source: Getty Images.

Palantir Technologies: 60% downside implied by Jefferies' target price

Palantir develops data analytics and artificial intelligence (AI) platforms to help customers in the public and private sectors integrate data, identify actionable insights, and automate work. Forrester Research recently ranked Palantir as a leader in AI platforms, and Sanjit Singh at Morgan Stanley sees Palantir emerging as the standard in enterprise AI.

The bull case centers around unique software. Whereas traditional analytics tools feature dashboards that tell clients what is happening, Palantir goes further. Its software revolves around a decision-making framework that helps customers decide what should happen next, and it lets them execute actions within the platform.

Palantir is also popular for providing flexibility and supporting privacy. Its AI platform gives customers the freedom to deploy the large language models of their choosing and swap between models without rewriting underlying applications. Palantir's software also includes governance controls that ensure business data is never fed back to model developers.

The bear case for Palantir is entirely focused on its valuation. Despite impressive financial results -- revenue increase 93% in the second quarter, the 12th consecutive acceleration -- Palantir currently trades at 78 times sales, making it the most expensive stock in the S&P 500 by a wide margin. The next closest contender is CrowdStrike at 50 times sales.

Indeed, Brent Thill says Palantir has excellent fundamentals, but the valuation simply does not make sense. He also thinks the company may be underinvesting in future growth, citing its high margins as evidence. But Thill is in the minority on Wall Street, as most analysts think the stock is undervalued. Palantir has a median target price of $223 per share, implying 12% upside from its current share price of $199.

Story Continues

Personally, I think Palantir is an excellent company with strong growth prospects, but whether it can grow fast enough to justify the current valuation is debatable. That makes the stock risky, so investors should keep their positions small. It is possible that Palantir could lose 60% of its value in the next year.

Super Micro Computer: 55% downside implied by Susquehanna's target price

Super Micro Computer assembles high-performance servers and other equipment used in data centers. Its products help businesses run demanding workloads, such as cloud services and AI applications. The company works closely with semiconductor companies like AMD and Nvidia to build servers featuring the latest CPUs and GPUs.

The bull case for Super Micro centers on immense demand for AI infrastructure. The five largest hyperscalers are forecast to spend $800 billion on capital expenditures in 2026, the vast majority of which will support AI compute capacity, according to Goldman Sachs . And analysts think that figure could hit $1.1 trillion in 2027.

The bear case for Super Micro centers on profitability. There is nothing particularly unique about the company, meaning it may lack a durable competitive advantage that protects its pricing power. Indeed, gross margin declined from 13.8% in fiscal 2024 to 11.1% in fiscal 2025 to 10.8% in fiscal 2025 despite tremendous demand for AI infrastructure.

Also, Super Micro has been at the center of two major controversies in recent years. In 2024, short-seller Hindenburg Research accused the company of financial manipulation and highlighted problems with corporate governance and export controls. In 2026, the latter allegations gained credibility when federal prosecutors charged three individuals associated with Super Micro with conspiring to divert $2.5 billion in AI servers to China.

Importantly, while the accounting irregularities Hindenburg highlighted have never been substantiated, weakness in corporate governance and internal export controls pose major risks to investors even without proof of deliberate financial fraud. Susquehanna analyst Mehdi Hosseini says the situation "underscores the urgency" of replacing CEO Charles Liang.

Super Micro currently trades at 11 times earnings, a seemingly reasonable valuation for a company whose earnings are forecast to increase at 23% annually over the next three years. Nevertheless, I think investors should avoid Super Micro. Not only does the company lack a durable competitive advantage, but past problems with weak corporate governance leave room for unpleasant surprises in the future.

news.Title: 台股季線測完「要攻5萬了」？ 法人拋出2劇本：快買3族群
news.Content:
台股今（28）日出現反彈，尾盤收漲939點，以47035點作收、收復季線，不過，分析師郭經緯提醒，指數想進一步挑戰5萬點，仍得面對前波高點48500點的套牢賣壓，除了站穩季線，成交量能否有效放大也是關鍵。他也點出後市2種可能走勢，建議未進場的投資人可以留意3大族群的布局機會。

台股近日自高點49K回落後，便在季線上下遊走，國泰期貨證期分析師郭經緯說明，台股今日大漲近千點，不僅收復季線，也為後續行情帶來轉機，唯一美中不足的是，指數上漲成交量卻量縮至7233億，接下來有11月初美國期中選舉不確定性、美國超級財報週與超級央行週等變數，令資金觀望情緒濃厚。

台股後市2劇本曝光

至於投資人關注的後市走向，郭經緯分析，第一是直接噴出10%並補量至逾9000億，消化套牢區直攻5萬點；第二是在美國期中選舉前震盪，維持7~8000億量能區間墊高，待選舉不確定性消除後再迎年底行情。

還沒上車可看「3族群」

郭經緯提到，投資人若還未上車，可以鎖定「3族群」，分別為：權值股台積電、聯發科、台達電；AI伺服器概念股如奇鋐、景碩、金像電；還有CPO光通訊族群，大立光、聯亞等。

郭經緯也建議，投資人可以先用3成資金低接權值領頭羊，若後續補量逾9000億，加碼至6到7成；若成交量量縮，則將資金控在5成以下。

news.Title: Global stocks get AI lift ahead of packed 48 hours
news.Content:
By Amanda Cooper

LONDON, Oct 28 (Reuters) - Global stocks rose on Wednesday, boosted by renewed enthusiasm over AI ahead of earnings from industry bellwethers later on, while in Europe, financial shares weighed on the broader market on a big day for results and oil rallied.

The ‌coming 48 hours are packed with potentially market-moving events, including rate decisions from major central banks including the Federal Reserve, European Central Bank and ‌Bank of Japan, as well as results from some of the beacons of the AI trade, such as Microsoft and Alphabet.

New Zealand's central bank delivered the first major surprise of the next couple ​of days by leaving interest rates on hold, contrary to expectations for a hike, triggering the biggest daily drop in the currency in five months .

Back on the equity market, Europe's STOXX was down 0.2%, pulled lower by a decline in shares of Banco Santander, UBS and a 12% slide in the stock of payments company Adyen.

MSCI's All-World index, meanwhile, was up 0.2%, as US stock futures edged up between 0.1% and 0.4% and stocks in Asia rallied, led by a 6% surge in South Korea's Kospi ‌after blockbuster earnings from chipmaker SK Hynix.

The AI rally faces ⁠its next test when technology giants Alphabet and Microsoft report earnings after the market close on Wednesday. Investors will be scouring for evidence of returns that would justify the hefty cost of the AI build-out.

"Investors want to see how these two mega-cap ⁠tech stocks are monetising their AI investments," XTB director Kathleen Brooks said.

"These results could determine if the tech/AI rally has legs. Any signs of 1, a failure to monetise investments, or 2, a slowdown in capex spend, could have big repercussions for the AI trade on Wednesday night and Thursday," she said.

A series of AI-related funding announcements from Meta, ​SpaceX ​and Broadcom this week has breathed new life into the AI trade, with Anthropic's filing ​for an initial public offering also providing support.

"Not all big ‌tech stocks should be treated equally regarding future potential growth. The period of a rising market lifting all stocks has started to shift," said Chris Brigati, SWBC's chief investment officer.

CENTRAL BANK SURPRISES

Beyond earnings, investors are awaiting the Bank of Canada and the Fed's respective policy decisions later on Wednesday.

Expectations are for the BoC to raise rates and the Fed to keep them unchanged, though analysts at JPMorgan said in a note they anticipate at least two dissents from US policymakers, which could send a hawkish signal to markets.

Story Continues

Earlier on Wednesday, the Reserve Bank of New Zealand surprised investors by keeping interest rates at 2.75% in a narrow vote, ‌sending the kiwi down more than 1.2% to a session low of $0.5583.

"Today's decision shows the ​RBNZ is willing to surprise markets, a reminder that central banks do not take orders from ​markets," Carol Kong, a currency strategist at Commonwealth Bank of Australia, ​said.

In the UK, finance minister John Healey will deliver a cautious first budget on Wednesday, one that prioritises stability in the ‌bond market over the kind of big spending moves that Andy ​Burnham talked about when he became prime ​minister.

The pound was down a touch at $1.3293, while UK government bond yields edged up 2 basis points to 5.363%, as prices dipped. Gilt yields are heading for their first monthly decline since June this month, down 7 bps.

Israel's shekel fell 1% after exit polls showed the country's wartime election ​appeared deadlocked.

Elsewhere, oil prices rose after an attack on a ‌refinery in Saudi Arabia, the world's biggest crude exporter, renewed concerns around the risks to supply in the Middle East. [O/R]

Brent crude futures ​were up 1.2% at $115.24 a barrel, while European natural gas futures rose to fresh four-year highs, up another 1.1% at €97.08 per MWh.

(Additional reporting ​by Rae Wee in Singapore; Editing by Christopher Cushing, Kate Mayberry, Toby Chopra)

news.Title: Warren Buffett’s Favorite Market Gauge Has Blown Past a Level He Once Called a Warning. History Says This Comes Next.
news.Content:
"You are playing with fire."

Warren Buffett used those five words to bluntly warn investors in a 2001 Fortune article. He preceded the warning with a discussion of his favorite market gauge, the ratio of total stock market capitalization to gross national product (GNP). This metric became popularly known as the Buffett indicator.

Missed AI's "Act 1"? Act 2 Could Be 14x Bigger. Most investors think they missed the AI boat because they didn't buy Nvidia in 2005. But according to our analysts, we're only at the end of "Act 1"—the R&D phase. "Act 2" is the global rollout. Continue »

The "Oracle of Omaha" wrote in the article that when the total stock market capitalization-to-GNP ratio "rose to an unprecedented level" nearly two years earlier, it "should have been a very strong warning signal" to investors. And he used the "playing with fire" language to describe the scenario when the market valuation gauge approaches 200%.

The Buffett indicator has now blown past that 200% level. History is crystal clear about what's likely to come next.

Warren Buffett. Image source: Getty Images. Image source: Getty Images.

The Buffett indicator's potentially dangerous surge

Buffett initially used GNP in the market valuation indicator that now bears his name. Over time, though, gross domestic product (GDP) replaced GNP. The two metrics both track a country's economic output. However, GNP reflects the value of all finished goods and services produced by a country's citizens, wherever they are, either at home or in another country. GDP only includes the value of the finished goods and services produced within a country's borders.

GNP and GDP track closely enough that it doesn't matter which one is used in the Buffett indicator. For example, the U.S. GNP today stands at $32,559,355,000,000, while the U.S. GDP is $32,563,030,000,000. A difference of around $3.7 billion doesn't matter much when both figures top $32.5 trillion.

Whichever economic metric you use, the Buffett indicator has surged to an all-time high. Using the Wilshire 5000 index as a proxy for total U.S. stock market capitalization, Buffett's favorite market gauge now hovers near 237%.

History's brutal lessons

The Buffett indicator has risen significantly above its long-term moving average three times over the past 100 years. The first instance was in the late 1920s. What happened next? The stock market crash of October 1929.

Buffett alluded to the second example of the ratio of total U.S. stock market capitalization to GNP surging in his 2001 Fortune article. In the late 1990s, the valuation metric hit an all-time high.

Story Continues

Soon afterward, the stock market plunged as the dot-com bubble burst. It took years for the S&P 500 (SNPINDEX:^GSPC) to regain its previous high.

The third case isn't quite as dramatic as the first two, but the pattern is still there. In late 2021, the Buffett indicator approached 200%. Were investors "playing with fire" then, as Buffett warned two decades earlier? Yep. The S&P 500 entered a bear market only weeks later, with the index sinking 19% the following year.

Three things investors can do

With Buffett using an analogy of fire, you might think that the smartest move is to get away from the fire altogether. In practical terms, that would mean selling all of your stocks and staying on the sidelines.

However, that isn't what Buffett is doing. He's still Berkshire Hathaway 's (NYSE:BRKA) (NYSE:BRKB) single biggest investor. He has been involved in the conglomerate's investing activity this year. And Berkshire still has hundreds of billions of dollars invested in stocks.

What should investors do if running for the hills isn't the best option? The first and simplest approach is to wait. Over the long run, the stock market generates positive returns.

Second, investors can build cash to be in a position to take advantage of a potential stock market downturn. Buffett has been doing this for a while, as evidenced by Berkshire's cash stockpile of nearly $385 billion.

Third, investors can buy stocks that are likely to successfully navigate market turbulence. Some healthcare stocks, for example, tend to hold up well even when the overall market declines.

Finally, it's important to remember that history doesn't always repeat itself. Just because the stock market has fallen sharply on previous occasions when the Buffett indicator rose to elevated levels doesn't necessarily mean that it will do so this time. But it doesn't hurt to be prepared just in case.

Missed AI's "Act 1"? Act 2 Could Be 14x Bigger

Most investors think they missed the AI boat because they didn't buy Nvidia in 2005.

But according to our analysts, we're only at the end of "Act 1"—the R&D phase. "Act 2" is the global rollout, a massive technology build-out that Google's CEO says could be more profound than fire or electricity.

While everyone watches the chip designers, one "backbone" company provides the critical technology that Nvidia and AMD literally cannot function without. We've detailed this under-the-radar player in our new AI Playbook.

Continue »

news.Title: Nvidia vs TSMC: Here’s Which One May Be the Biggest AI Winner.
news.Content:
Nvidia (NASDAQ:NVDA) and Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing (NYSE:TSM) each have emerged as major players in the artificial intelligence (AI) space. Nvidia designs the graphics processing units (GPUs) crucial to major AI tasks, and TSMC manufactures these chips. These companies have seen revenue explode higher, and their stock prices have followed, advancing more than 400% and 300%, respectively, over three years.

They clearly are well-positioned to excel as this AI story unfolds. But which of the two might be the biggest AI winner? Let's take a close look at each business and find out.

Missed AI's "Act 1"? Act 2 Could Be 14x Bigger. Most investors think they missed the AI boat because they didn't buy Nvidia in 2005. But according to our analysts, we're only at the end of "Act 1"—the R&D phase. "Act 2" is the global rollout. Continue »

Image source: Getty Images.

The case for Nvidia

Nvidia isn't the only company to design GPUs , but it is the market leader. This is for a few reasons. Nvidia saw the AI opportunity about a decade ago and jumped in, designing its GPUs specifically for this use. This early start offered it the chance to fine-tune its technology and develop relationships with key customers. Today, Nvidia's commitment to annual innovation keeps it in the No. 1 spot -- as rivals develop a GPU to beat the current Nvidia product, Nvidia has already moved on to its next update.

This AI powerhouse, thanks to its CUDA parallel computing platform and vast array of products and services, offers customers everything to suit their AI needs. These customers, already using Nvidia platforms, might find it easier and more cost-effective to stick with this provider, building on systems they already have operating.

Nvidia's premium product and full-stack advantage mean it can charge premium prices, offering it fantastic margins. The company's gross margin consistently tops 70%, and this is on sales that keep climbing to record highs. In the recent quarter, revenue jumped 106% to $96 billion.

All of this has made Nvidia an obvious superstar of the AI revolution.

The case for TSMC

TSMC wins when Nvidia wins. This is because it manufactures Nvidia's chips, so high demand for them equals more revenue for TSMC. But this company also wins when Nvidia's rivals see strong chip demand. This is because TSMC dominates the pure foundry market -- holding more than 70% share, according to Counterpoint Research.

This manufacturing giant makes chips for most of the major players, from Advanced Micro Devices to Broadcom . So, if you invest in TSMC, you don't have to worry about which chipmaker or cloud service provider will prevail. Chances are, TSMC will benefit no matter which player takes the lead. This makes TSMC a rather "safe" AI stock.

Story Continues

All of this has translated into growth for the manufacturer. In the latest earnings update, TSMC reported its sixth straight quarter of record profit, and revenue and net income surpassed analysts' estimates. Still, revenue of $46 billion for the period is low compared with Nvidia's. It's important to keep in mind that while TSMC is benefiting from the AI boom, it incurs the high cost of manufacturing overhead -- from facilities to expensive equipment -- to keep up. Nvidia doesn't face such costs, and since it sells a premium product to end customers, it may more freely charge high prices.

Which stock will emerge as the biggest winner?

It's clear that Nvidia and TSMC are benefiting from this AI boom, and they are also likely to continue generating growth as the AI story unfolds. Though the companies have delivered impressive revenue gains in recent years, AI is just entering real-world use. And this means the revenue increases may continue for quite some time.

TSMC holds the advantage of benefiting from all of the chip designers' successes. That's a big plus. But Nvidia's pricing power and market dominance -- which it should maintain thanks to its innovation -- may keep this company a step ahead in terms of growth in the years to come. So while both of these players are likely to be ongoing AI success stories, Nvidia -- and its investors -- might score the biggest win.

news.Title: Would An AI Stock Crash Be as Bad as 2008? Here's What "Big Short" Investor Steve Eisman Says.
news.Content: Steve Eisman, whose character was played by Steve Carell in the movie "The Big Short," recently appeared on The Compound and Friends podcast. Many people look to Eisman's analysis to evaluate risks facing the market. He got famous as one of the investors who predicted the 2008 housing market crash. But Eisman doesn't think we're on the verge of a comparable crisis. In recent months, some investors have grown nervous about artificial intelligence (AI) stocks. They question whether AI is going to pay off for investors, or if major tech companies are spending too much (and taking on too much debt) to build data centers and develop expensive AI models. Could this be the start of another dot-com crash, or another financial crisis? Missed AI's "Act 1"? Act 2 Could Be 14x Bigger. Most investors think they missed the AI boat because they didn't buy Nvidia in 2005. But according to our analysts, we're only at the end of "Act 1"—the R&D phase. "Act 2" is the global rollout. Continue » On the podcast, Eisman said, "If you want to draw parallels to the great financial crisis, there's a big difference" with what's going on now in AI stocks . Let's look at what Eisman thinks about today's AI stock market boom and why long-term investors don't need to panic -- even if they feel more cautious about the tech sector. Why the 2008 stock market crash was so bad Here's the thing a lot of younger investors who weren't involved in the stock market during 2008 might not know: That was an exceptionally terrible stock market crash, probably the worst economic crisis of my lifetime. Here's what happened to the S&P 500 index (SNPINDEX: ^GSPC) in 2008: ^SPX data by YCharts Why was 2008 so bad? Major investment banks, like Bear Stearns and Lehman Brothers, failed. Investors suddenly realized that too much of the economy had been propped up by bad mortgage debt. Too many homeowners suddenly couldn't afford to pay their debts after interest rates rose. Too many big banks made big bets on the housing market, with the idea that the industry was just going to keep growing. These big bets ultimately went bust. When people lose trust in the financial system, the entire economy can collapse. That doesn't seem to be the case with the AI boom. Eisman: AI is more like General Motors than JPMorgan In his podcast interview, Eisman explained how there are a few different levels and sizes of economic crises that can cause recessions. He gave this hypothetical example: What if a major employer like General Motors goes bankrupt? Story Continues If a big company like General Motors goes out of business, it causes a lot of pain. People lose their jobs. There might be a local or regional recession within the economies of the cities and states where that company has a lot of employees and suppliers. But even though a bankruptcy of that size would be bad for the economy, it still would be nowhere near as bad as 2008. In 2008, major banks failed or were on the verge of failure. The government had to bail out the banks to prevent the financial system from collapsing. This was much worse than GM going out of business; this could have become a new Great Depression -- or worse. On the podcast, Eisman gave another hypothetical example of a globally systemically important bank like JPMorgan Chase going bankrupt. As Eisman said, if a big company like GM goes down, it's bad. But he also said: When JPMorgan goes down, planet Earth burns. That's the end. The reason the government had to bail everybody out was you can't have a situation where people can't get their money out of the bank. Eisman said the possible AI bubble is more like the General Motors example. Even if the AI boom turns out to be disappointing, even if it goes bust and the stock market crashes, Eisman doesn't believe this would be as bad as 2008 because as he said, "The banks are fine." How to invest for an AI stock crash It's possible that the recent AI-related boom in the stock market will keep going for a while longer. The biggest tech companies on Earth are trying to build the must-have business tools and consumer apps of the future. If AI pays off, the rewards for investors could be life-changing. If you believe that the future of AI is bright and that we're still in the early days of the AI revolution, if you believe that the biggest winners from the future of AI will be the tech companies that are building AI and aggressively adopting AI tools today, buying tech ETFs could be a good move. The Invesco Nasdaq QQQ ETF (NASDAQ: QQQM) lets you own the entire tech-heavy Nasdaq-100 for a low expense ratio of 0.15%. But if you're worried that AI is a little overhyped and overpriced, if you feel like other parts of the economy might do better in the future than just a few tech majors, you might want to invest in a broad stock market index fund like the Vanguard S&P 500 ETF (NYSEMKT: VOO) with a super low expense ratio of just 0.03%. A possible AI stock sell-off could still hurt the S&P 500, but the downturn might be less severe than in a tech ETF. In the long run, buying the entire S&P 500 tends to be a solid move -- even if there are a few sell-offs and bear markets along the way. Missed AI's "Act 1"? Act 2 Could Be 14x Bigger Most investors think they missed the AI boat because they didn't buy Nvidia in 2005. But according to our analysts, we're only at the end of "Act 1"—the R&D phase. "Act 2" is the global rollout, a massive technology build-out that Google's CEO says could be more profound than fire or electricity. While everyone watches the chip designers, one "backbone" company provides the critical technology that Nvidia and AMD literally cannot function without. We've detailed this under-the-radar player in our new AI Playbook. Continue » JPMorgan Chase is an advertising partner of Motley Fool Money. Ben Gran has no position in any of the stocks mentioned. The Motley Fool has positions in and recommends JPMorgan Chase and Vanguard S&P 500 ETF. The Motley Fool recommends General Motors. The Motley Fool has a disclosure policy . news.Title: Why Alphabet’s Own AI Chips May Be Its Quietest Advantage
news.Content:
Nvidia is the company best known for artificial intelligence (AI) chips, and that's because its graphics processing units (GPUs) have powered the training of the world's top models. And as a result, earnings have soared. But a quieter chip story is unfolding at Alphabet (NASDAQ:GOOG)(NASDAQ:GOOGL), and investors may just begin to see it in the company's financial results.

Alphabet has spent years designing its own AI chips, known as tensor processing units, or TPUs. For most of that time, these chips mainly served Google's own products and its cloud customers. This year, though, Alphabet started selling TPU systems directly to customers who want to run them in their own data centers.

Missed AI's "Act 1"? Act 2 Could Be 14x Bigger. Most investors think they missed the AI boat because they didn't buy Nvidia in 2005. But according to our analysts, we're only at the end of "Act 1"—the R&D phase. "Act 2" is the global rollout. Continue »

So, why might the TPU be Alphabet's quietest advantage? Let's find out.

Image source: Getty Images.

From AI worry to AI winner

First, a quick look at how Alphabet got here. Not long ago, some investors worried the company would be a casualty of the AI era , with the idea that chatbots would pull users away from Google Search -- if that happened, it would clearly hurt advertising, which is Alphabet's bread and butter. Those worries haven't played out. In the second quarter, Google Search revenue grew 17%, and Google advertising represented 68% of total revenue.

Meanwhile, Google Cloud, the company's cloud computing arm, has been picking up serious momentum, with revenue advancing 63% in the first quarter and then 82% in the second, to reach more than $24 billion. And the cloud backlog, which represents contracted commitments not yet recognized as revenue, hit $514 billion, with just over half expected to convert to revenue within 24 months.

Where the TPU fits in

Here's where the chip comes in. Unlike a general-purpose chip, a TPU is designed with AI workloads in mind, and Alphabet has refined the technology across multiple generations. That gives the company two potential benefits. First, it can run its own AI services and those of its cloud customers on hardware it controls, rather than relying solely on Nvidia's supply and pricing. Second, it can now sell that hardware as a product.

Earlier this year, Alphabet announced that it would start selling "multiple gigawatts of TPU hardware" to a select group of customers for use in their data centers, and in the second quarter, Alphabet recognized revenue from TPU system sales for the first time. Management said it's still a small piece for now, with most of the revenue expected in 2027. A Citizens analyst in a May note said the company may deliver around $3 billion of revenue from TPU-related infrastructure this year and $25 billion next year, according to Fortune.

Story Continues

This doesn't mean Alphabet is on track to replace Nvidia or other major chip designers. Nvidia and direct peers built a dominant business by selling chips broadly across the market. Alphabet, through its TPU business, has a chance to build a second profit stream on top of an already thriving cloud and advertising business -- it doesn't have to win over the entire chip market.

What to watch

Of course, there are risks. TPU sales are early, and as mentioned, most of the revenue won't start flowing in until next year. To support some of these agreements, Alphabet has agreed to provide credit backstops for third-party data centers and power infrastructure -- this adds a layer of financial risk. Developers also remain highly committed to Nvidia's ecosystem, so Alphabet's chips will have to keep proving themselves.

Still, this new step in the AI chip market is positive for Alphabet. The tech giant has a fast-growing cloud unit, a resilient and leading search business, and now a chip business that offers more control over costs and a new source of revenue. All of this reinforces the buy case for Alphabet amid this ongoing AI story.

news.Title: 國城：台南房市明年有望反彈　台積電員工進場購屋
news.Content:
（中央社記者何秀玲台南2026年10月28日電）國城建設創辦人洪平森表示，台南房市經近年修正，目前已處相對低點，在經濟成長、股市熱絡等因素支撐下，明年房價有機會向上彈升。國城在台南平實重劃區最大公辦都更案，受惠於台南科學園區科技新貴購屋需求，約35%至40%買方為科技業，包括台積電員工。

國城建設今天舉行台南東區平實特區大型公辦都更案二期公開記者會。洪平森接受媒體訪問表示，台灣經濟表現佳，加上股市熱絡，對房市形成支撐，先前央行祭出房市管制措施讓房地產市場暫時停滯，目前房市景氣已處於低點，預期明年或後年有望看到反彈，但房市何時出現明確轉折點難以預測。

洪平森說，台南過去幾年部分區域房價漲幅較大，目前市場屬於修正，部分蛋白區房價修正屬合理現象，加上近年央行祭出房市管制措施，台南房價有望逐步恢復理性走勢。

國城主管表示，平實特區公辦都更案基地面積約8600坪，整體分3期開發，目前已進入第2期。隨台積電持續擴大台南先進製程布局，科技業購屋需求受到關注。國城主管表示，目前科技業族群約占買方35%至40%，其中包括台積電員工，但部分客戶較為低調，僅能掌握主要來自電子科技業。

觀察購屋客群，國城主管表示，目前投資客已大幅退場，案場以換屋、自住需求為主，首購族占比較低；台南在地買方占逾7成，其餘近3成來自其他縣市。此案產品以中大坪數為主，3房約占7成、2房約占3成，主要坪數為25坪、37坪及45坪。

news.Title: Zacks Investment Ideas feature highlights: Teradyne, Lam Research and ATI
news.Content:
For Immediate Release

Chicago, IL – October 28, 2026– Today, Zacks Investment Ideas feature highlights Teradyne TER, Lam Research LRCX and ATI Inc. ATI.

Equities Bounce: 3 Top Ranked Stocks to Buy Now (TER, LRCX, ATI)

After a sharp bout of volatility, the stock market appears to be finding its footing ahead of a busy week of corporate earnings, central bank meetings and critical economic data.

While these selloffs can be painful, it is worth remembering just how consistently the market manages to climb the proverbial wall of worry. Whether it's concerns over AI, tariffs, elections or geopolitical tensions, the resilience of the US stock market has been remarkable.

And while it can be tempting to follow every headline and attempt to anticipate every possible scenario, investors are often better served by tuning out the noise and focusing on what matters most: buying high-quality companies at attractive valuations, particularly when earnings expectations are moving higher.

That combination of strong fundamentals, reasonable valuations and positive earnings revisions has historically been a powerful formula for long-term investment success.

With that in mind, three stocks currently stand out to me as particularly compelling opportunities. Teradyne , Lam Research and ATI Inc. are established industry leaders with impressive long-term track records, favorable earnings revision trends and exposure to powerful secular growth opportunities.

All three have delivered tremendous returns over the years, but recent market volatility has created potentially attractive entry points for investors looking to capitalize on the next leg higher.

Teradyne Stock: Exceptional Growth at a Fair Price

Teradyne is a leading provider of automated test equipment used to verify the performance and reliability of semiconductors, along with advanced robotics systems for industrial automation. The company is a major beneficiary of the AI infrastructure boom, as increasingly sophisticated chips and memory components require more extensive testing.

The growth outlook is exceptional. Analysts expect sales to surge 58.9% this year, followed by another 20.9% increase next year. Meanwhile, earnings are projected to grow at an annualized rate of 54.4% over the next three to five years.

Despite that tremendous growth outlook, Teradyne trades at 33.9x forward earnings, giving it a remarkably attractive PEG ratio of just 0.62 . That suggests investors are paying a relatively modest premium for the company's anticipated earnings growth.

Story Continues

With a Zacks Rank #1 (Strong Buy) , Teradyne offers a compelling combination of powerful secular tailwinds, explosive earnings growth and a valuation that looks increasingly reasonable following the recent pullback.

Lam Research Stock: A Semiconductor Powerhouse

Lam Research is one of the world's leading suppliers of semiconductor manufacturing equipment, specializing in the technologies used to deposit, etch and clean materials on silicon wafers. Its equipment is essential to producing advanced logic chips and memory, making Lam a critical supplier to the ongoing AI infrastructure expansion.

The company is particularly well positioned to benefit from the memory supercycle, as demand for high-bandwidth memory and increasingly complex chip architectures drives greater investment in semiconductor manufacturing equipment.

Analysts expect sales to grow 49.7% this year and another 19% next year, while earnings are projected to compound at an annualized rate of 28.2% over the next three to five years.

Even with that impressive growth profile, Lam trades at just 24.8x forward earnings , giving it a PEG ratio of 0.88. For a company with such an entrenched competitive position and exposure to one of the market's strongest investment themes, that valuation looks attractive.

Lam currently carries a Zacks Rank #2 (Buy) , reinforcing its favorable earnings outlook and making it another compelling opportunity for long-term investors.

ATI Stock: Aerospace Growth at a Compelling Valuation

ATI INC is a leading producer of high-performance specialty materials, including titanium alloys, nickel-based superalloys and advanced components used in aerospace, defense and other demanding industrial applications.

The company occupies an attractive position in the aerospace supply chain, providing critical materials used in jet engines, aircraft structures and defense systems. Rising commercial aircraft production, growing defense spending and demand for next-generation engines create a long runway for growth.

ATI's earnings outlook is particularly impressive, with analysts forecasting annualized EPS growth of 32.8% over the next three to five years.

Shares currently trade at 32.1x forward earnings, giving the stock a PEG ratio just below 1.0 . While that earnings multiple might initially appear elevated for an industrial company, the anticipated growth rate makes the valuation considerably more attractive.

ATI also carries a Zacks Rank #1 (Strong Buy) , reflecting positive earnings estimate revisions and strengthening expectations for the business.

Should Investors Buy Shares in LRCX, ATI and TER?

Market volatility can be unsettling, but it also creates opportunities to buy exceptional businesses at more attractive prices.

Teradyne, Lam Research and ATI operate in different corners of the economy, yet all three share several important characteristics: strong competitive positions, exposure to durable secular growth trends and impressive long-term earnings prospects.

More importantly, their valuations appear reasonable relative to their projected earnings growth, with all three sporting PEG ratios below 1.0.

Of course, none is immune to a broader market correction, and those ambitious growth forecasts will need to be met. But with favorable Zacks Ranks, powerful industry tailwinds and compelling growth-adjusted valuations, TER, LRCX and ATI deserve serious consideration from investors looking to take advantage of the recent market volatility.
